item.title: Malaysia Vows to Keep Taiwan Trade Ties While Sticking to ‘One China’
item.description: Malaysia wants to maintain strong economic ties with Taiwan while remaining firmly committed to its “One-China” policy, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.
item.dc:creator: Kok Leong Chan and Danial Azhar

item.title: Patience Is Paying Off for Chevron in Venezuela
item.description:
Chevron has been operating in Venezuela since 1923, and remained in the country while many US energy companies left. CFO Eimear Bonner and CEO Mike Wirth discuss the new terms of Chevron's joint venture that's projected to double production in Venezuela over the next five years. They speak to Annmarie Hordern on "Chief Future Officer."
(Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Fallout Puts Trade Truce to the Test as Xi Welcomes Trump
item.description: Xi Jinping’s third summit of the year with Donald Trump is going off script before their meetings even get underway, as the spy allegations engulfing Nvidia Corp.’s Jensen Huang reopen old rifts.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Nvidia Preparing to Oust CEO Jensen Huang: WSJ
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Suzan DelBene says there should be an investigation into Nvidia and Jensen Huang to understand potential national security implications. Kevin Brady, former Republican Congressman from Texas, says Democrats are effectively in control of the timing and content of government funding legislation during the lame-duck session as control of the House changes hands. Gregory Allen, Founder and CEO of Decision Tree Research, says Nvidia is not structured to easily absorb the loss of Jensen Huang and argues the company has been built around Huang’s leadership without a clear successor. Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) says Jensen Huang should be subpoenaed if he does not appear for a requested voluntary interview with lawmakers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Administration Unveils New Plan to Sell Federal Lands
item.description: The Trump administration has formally unveiled plans to sell public land as part of a new strategy laying out Interior Department goals.
item.dc:creator: Ari Natter

item.title: How a Jensen Huang Ousting Could Impact Broader Markets
item.description: Romaine Bostick gives us a look at how an ousting of Jensen Huang could not only impact Nvidia's stock price, but also competitors and broader markets. He spoke with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Krishnamoorthi Says Huang Should Face Subpoena
item.description: Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) says Jensen Huang should be subpoenaed if he does not appear for a requested voluntary interview with lawmakers. Rep. Krishnamoorthi says Congress needs a classified intelligence briefing on what information may have been obtained by the alleged Chinese spy and whether Huang was involved in any illicit activity. Rep. Krishnamoorthi says lawmakers must strengthen US export-control laws during the lame-duck session and says he is confident colleagues will support moving expeditiously. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Brady Says Democrats Control Lame-Duck Funding Timing
item.description: Kevin Brady, former Republican Congressman from Texas, says Democrats are effectively in control of the timing and content of government funding legislation during the lame-duck session as control of the House changes hands. Brady says he expects lawmakers to extend government funding rather than allow a shutdown, although the timing remains unsettled. Brady says divided government could create opportunities for bipartisan tax policy, including IRS reforms and changes related to the 2025 tax law. Brady says Democrats are also likely to pursue restoration of renewable-energy, child and health-care tax credits while proposing higher taxes on corporations and individuals. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. DelBene: Nvidia, Huang Should Face Investigation
item.description: Rep. Suzan DelBene says there should be an investigation into Nvidia and Jensen Huang to understand potential national security implications. Rep. DelBene says Democrats will conduct oversight of the Trump administration when they take control of the House and require administration officials to appear before Congress and follow laws enacted by lawmakers. Rep. DelBene says Democrats will focus on high costs and health care and will work across the aisle with Republicans willing to support those priorities. She speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Midterm Elections 2026: Democratic Wins Across South to Reshape Strategy
item.description: Democrats made historic gains with voters in the Southern US. Now the party needs to figure out how to keep them.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson, Ellen Milligan and Emily Birnbaum

item.title: Nvidia Is a 'Story of Hubris,' Decision Tree CEO Says
item.description: Gregory Allen, Decision Tree Research CEO and founder, reacts to the Wall Street Journal report that Nvidia is planning to oust CEO Jensen Huang. He speaks on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Preparing to Oust CEO Jensen Huang: WSJ
item.description: Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who is reportedly suspected of being a Chinese spy, the Wall Street Journal said Wednesday. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Germany Delays New Taxes, Power-Tax Cut, Rolls Back Welfare Cuts
item.description: The parties in Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s ruling coalition rolled back some planned social-spending cuts and delayed new taxes, clearing the way for a deal on Germany’s 2027 budget.
item.dc:creator: Kamil Kowalcze

item.title: Big Take: Huang's Scandal Will Push Democrats on US-China Policy
item.description: Today’s Big Take podcast digs into the geopolitical legacy President Trump is trying to cement in his final two years in office, even as a new majority Democratic Congress aims to rein him in on trade and foreign intervention. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: CoreWeave Triggers Rally
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
A gauge for emerging-market stocks rose for a third day, led by Asian chipmakers, as strong CoreWeave sales and signs of demand for Anthropic’s planned IPO fueled optimism over AI spending. CoreWeave shares gain as much as 18%, in biggest jump since August, after the cloud-computing provider boosts its annual revenue forecast. Analysts said the results ease worries about the company’s financing, although concerns remain.
On today’s episode:
Brody Ford, Bloomberg News Tech Reporter Bailey Lipschultz, Bloomberg News Senior IPO Reporter Jenny Rooke, Genoa Ventures Founder & Managing Director (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: House Democrats Respond to White House Threat Over Coming Probes
item.description: House Democrats said Wednesday they wouldn't be intimidated or deterred by threats from President Trump's top lawyer over expected investigations in the next Congress. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Mississippi Voters Pick Another Senator to Widen Democratic Win
item.description: Democrats padded their US Senate majority with a surprise win by Scott Colom, a district attorney who ousted Mississippi Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in a reliably Republican state that President Donald Trump won by more than 22 percentage points in 2024.
item.dc:creator: Caitlin Reilly

item.title: Schumer Faces Progressive Push for Bolder Agenda After Midterm Rout
item.description: Some Democrats don’t give their Senate leader credit for their party’s electoral success.
item.dc:creator: Steven T. Dennis

item.title: DSA Saying ‘You’re Next’ to Jeffries Angers Black Democrats
item.description: Some of New York’s incoming congressional delegation aren’t sold on backing Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker of the House.
item.dc:creator: Laura Nahmias

item.title: Prabowo Said to Accept Indonesia Vice President Resignation
item.description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto has accepted the resignation of Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka, according to people with knowledge of the matter.
item.dc:creator: Chandra Asmara and Faris Mokhtar
